questions.subject: JEE Mathematics
questions.question_text: True or False: Every continuous function is differentiable everywhere.

answer_key.explanation: False -- e.g. f(x) = |x| is continuous everywhere but not differentiable at x=0.

questions.subject: JEE Mathematics
questions.question_text: True or False: A quadratic equation with real coefficients can have exactly one real root.

answer_key.explanation: True -- when the discriminant is zero, the equation has one repeated real root.

questions.subject: JEE Mathematics
questions.question_text: True or False: Matrix multiplication is commutative in general, i.e. AB = BA for all matrices A and B.

answer_key.explanation: False -- matrix multiplication is generally non-commutative; AB ≠ BA in most cases.

questions.subject: JEE Mathematics
questions.question_text: True or False: The sum of an infinite geometric series always converges regardless of the common ratio.

answer_key.explanation: False -- it converges only when the absolute value of the common ratio is less than 1.

questions.subject: JEE Mathematics
questions.question_text: Explain the geometric meaning of the derivative of a function at a point.

rubric_points: States the derivative gives the slope of the tangent line to the curve at that point
Explains it as the limit of the slope of secant lines as the second point approaches the first
Connects this to instantaneous rate of change of the function

questions.subject: JEE Mathematics
questions.question_text: Explain why the discriminant of a quadratic equation determines the nature of its roots.

rubric_points: Explains D>0 gives two distinct real roots, D=0 gives one repeated real root, D<0 gives complex roots
Connects this to the square root term in the quadratic formula being real, zero, or imaginary

questions.subject: JEE Mathematics
questions.question_text: Explain the difference between independent events and mutually exclusive events in probability.

rubric_points: Independent events: occurrence of one does not affect the probability of the other, P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B)
Mutually exclusive events: cannot occur at the same time, P(A∩B)=0
Notes that two events with nonzero probability can't be both independent and mutually exclusive
